subject: ACME — Context length & token volume follow-up
messages:
Date: 2026-07-15T15:02:00-07:00
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Jones <sam.jones@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Subject: Quick follow-up + next steps on token volumes & context length

Hi Sam — thanks again for the call today. Really helpful to hear about Acme's roadmap for using summarization + agentic assistants across product and support. Per our discussion, wanted to capture the key asks and next steps so we can size pricing and a pilot: 

Summary notes:
- Primary workload: multi-document summarization + contextual retrieval + short agentic actions.
- Expected Q3 volume: 5M–15M tokens/month initially; potential to ramp to ~50M tokens/month in 12 months.
- Latency expectation: p95 < 1.2s for 512-token completions; higher for long context retrieval.
- Security: need SOC2 + VPC peering for pilot (we discussed Private).

Questions we still need from you to finalize the pricing ballpark: 
1) Typical prompt length (avg prompt tokens) — examples? distribution across short (0–512), medium (513–4k), long (>4k).
2) Typical completion length (avg completion tokens) and variance.
3) How often you need extended context (8k vs 32k vs 128k) — % of requests that would target each.
4) Target $/1M tokens or budget range you have in mind for evaluation.

If you can attach a short sample profile (CSV is fine) with token counts by request type, that'll let us produce an accurate per-1M estimate and model/context recommendations. I've cc'd Rishi to loop in pricing & reserved-capacity options.

Proposed next steps:
- You share token profile sample (CSV).
- We return a 2-page pricing + model recommendation with three scenarios (hosted burst, reserved Dedicated, Private pilot).
- Schedule a 30-min pricing review next week.

Thanks — I'll hold time slots Tue/Wed next week; what works for you?

—
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — shared notes below and attached a quick token profile (CSV) from last month's sampling. High-level answers:

1) Prompt tokens (avg): 380 tokens overall. Distribution: ~60% short (0-512), ~30% medium (513-4k), ~10% long (>4k).
2) Completion tokens (avg): 220 tokens; most completions are 50–400 tokens, tail to ~2k for long summaries.
3) Extended context needs: about 6% of requests need 32k, ~1% need >32k (we can approximate as 128k for a small subset of analytics jobs).
4) Budget: We're aiming for $800–$1,500 per 1M tokens for eval/pilot (upper bound flexible if performance and tooling reduce net cost).

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + next steps on token volumes & context length

Perfect — thanks for the CSV, Sam. I dug into the high-level numbers and pulled together a quick ballpark based on the distribution you shared. See key takeaways below (ballpark, for planning only):

Assumptions (from your sample): avg prompt = 380, avg completion = 220 => avg total ~600 tokens/request. Current sample volume: 10M tokens/month => ~16.6k requests/day.

Ballpark unit economics (approx per 1M tokens):
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go): 
  - Baseline model mix: open Llama-like / optimized small -> estimated $1,200–$1,600 per 1M tokens (includes KV caching benefits for repeated prompts)
- Dedicated reserved (monthly commit): 
  - Committed economics: ~$850–$1,100 per 1M tokens depending on commit and burst profile
- Private (VPC/on-prem): 
  - Higher setup + infra; effective unit cost can drop to ~$600–900 per 1M tokens at 50M+ tokens/month with proper batching/quantization

Context length notes:
- ~60% short: will be low-cost and low-latency.
- ~30% medium: benefits from batching; pricing above assumes medium proportion.
- ~7% 32k-ish and ~1% 128k-ish: these drive storage and KV/cache sizing — add-on for long-context enabled endpoints.

Next asks for precise pricing: 
- Confirm target pilot budget (you mentioned $800–$1,500/1M) — where in that range would you aim?
- Any strict requirements for retention/ingestion (affects Private vs Hosted selection)?
- Do you expect to pin a model family for pilot (we can recommend a model mix if not).

I'm attaching our short pricing grid and will have Rishi add Dedicated commit options. If Tue 7/21 10am PT works, I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
—
Marissa

Sam — quick note from pricing/ops side. We can build a pilot that fits your $800–$1,500/1M target depending on commitment and model selection. Couple operational clarifications that will change the numbers materially: 

- Retention & logs: do you need indefinite request/response retention for debugging? (Adds storage and egress costs).
- KV cache hit expectations: if you have high repetition, effective token cost can drop 10–30%.
- SLA: Hosted SLOs differ from Dedicated/Private — if you need 99.95% with guaranteed latency p95, that will change the commit tiers.

If you can confirm retention & SLA expectations, we'll lock a recommended scenario (hosted vs reserved vs private) and provide a final per-1M estimate and an optional reserved tier (12-month contract) that hits your lower target.

Thanks — looping Logan to ensure we size the KV/cache and GPU pool correctly for 32k/128k usage.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

Thanks all — confirming details below so we can move to a pilot contract:

- Pilot budget target: $1,000 per 1M tokens (aiming for mid-point).
- Retention: 30 days of request/response logs retained, plus aggregated metrics indefinitely.
- SLA: p95 latency target 1.5s for short/medium; for long-context requests we can accept higher p95.
- Model pinning: no strict requirement for pilot; we want Redwood to recommend the model mix.
- 32k/128k usage: 32k about 6% of traffic; 128k jobs are one-off analytics (~0.5–1%); please size caching/storage accordingly.

Next steps: please send a one-page pilot SOW and pricing for the $1,000/1M target including an optional 3-month reserved commit that lowers unit cost. We can sign the SOW and kick off a 4-week pilot.

Sam
—
Sam Jones
